correctness.rationale: Invertible base adjacency makes the block-square vectors u_i linearly independent. On the intrinsic square space dual, the determinant of the multiplication pencil is a product of distinct linear factors ell(u_i) with exponents n_i, times a nonzero scalar in the normalized algebra. Unique factorization and the radicals at points on only one factor recover the block permutation and its dimensions. Independently, the rank of left multiplication by x equals the number of its nonzero block projections: each nonzero projection gives a surjective scalar functional on its block, independently of the others, with output along u_i. Thus the maximal subspaces of the rank-at-most-one locus are exactly the blocks, even over fields where nonzero vectors can have zero self-dot-product. Projecting the transported u_i across these blocks gives a graph automorphism and T(s_j)=c_i s_sigma(j) for each edge i~j. Evaluating the product identity on s_i twice gives k_i^2=d_i c_i because its norm n_i is nonzero. Even-walk connectedness forces a common scalar in the nonbipartite case, and one scalar per side in the bipartite case; solving the latter equations gives b^3=D_X^2 D_Y and a=b^2/D_X. Dividing T_i by k_i yields precisely a dot-product isometry preserving the block sum. Conversely these block maps satisfy the product identity; block coordinate maps supply an isometry for any allowed permutation. The specialization to complete multipartite graphs uses det Adj(K_t)=(-1)^(t-1)(t-1) and d_i=N-n_i. For K_{2,3}, 18 is indeed not a rational cube. Independent finite determinant enumeration and rational edge-equation checks gave 412 cases, 385 expanded-singular, eight degree-condition cases and six rational witnesses.
residual_risks: Finite tests do not exclude general non-diagonal maps; block recovery and the norm constraint prove this exclusion where the criterion fails. No claim extends to arbitrary singular quotients or positive characteristic.

value.rationale: A nonsingular false-twin quotient is an intrinsic and useful graph condition that allows expanded adjacency of unbounded corank. The theorem answers the singular-graph isomorphism question uniformly on that family rather than checking selected examples. Recovering the blocks controls maps not assumed monomial, and the distinction between real and rational isomorphism shows why the ground field cannot be omitted from the structural criterion.
residual_risks: The claim is a subcase of the general graph problem and does not by itself solve the singular-quotient or positive-characteristic cases.
